findings.summary: Install step 11b names no command for finding the guest's new address
findings.recommendation: instance: the closure boot can change the address and the runbook warns that `tart ip` may report the stale one, but it only says to read 'the host's ARP table for the softnet bridge' while every other step gives an exact command. Step 12's stability check starts from this address, so an operator guessing it could compare the wrong host. Consider giving the exact command (e.g. `arp -an` filtered to the softnet bridge interface) once the dry run confirms it; no change is required for merge.
findings.fix_cost: FIX is free WHERE THIS FINDING POINTS — every file it cites is non-judgeable, so an edit confined to those moves no coverage and buys no round. If the real correction lands elsewhere, price the actual batch with `cost-of-commit` first.

summary: 0 blocking, 0 warning, 1 note across 1 reviewer(s). Changes ready to proceed.
next_action: AT REVIEW TIME you were not making a judgeable commit (your tree was clean), so the first judgeable fix bought a whole review round. Re-derive with `prawduct-hook cost-of-commit` if the tree has moved since. Recommended while that holds: accept these unless a fix is worth that. 0 blocking — THE REVIEW IS OVER. The 0 warning + 1 note finding(s) gate NOTHING: no gate reads them, so nothing in THIS review requires another round. (Whether the PR gate is satisfied, and whether the work cycle still owes a final/cumulative, are separate questions about coverage — ask them by running the gate, not by reviewing again.) Disposition each finding instead of reflexively fixing it — accept is the default for anything nobody will realistically action: `prawduct-hook disposition rev-20260930T205606Z-234f20da <fid|oid> --accept "<reason>"`, which needs no review and moves no tree. If you do choose to fix some, batch them into ONE commit — and re-cover with ONE `/prawduct:critic verify-resolutions` ONLY if that commit touched judgeable files. AFTER committing, you no longer have to judge that either: dispatch asks the same predicate and exits 3 (`no review needed`, under a second, no session state written) rather than spending a reviewer on a free interval — so asking costs nothing, and a refusal is the answer, not a reason to retry in another mode. Do NOT start another round to 'close coverage' before committing, and do not infer that you need one from gate output printed before your fix — commit, then re-run the gate and let it answer. If this branch has more judgeable work coming, there is a third route: carry the fix into the NEXT chunk's commit. That is NOT the deferral warned against above — deferring to a later ROUND buys a second round; riding a commit that is being made anyway buys none. Write it where that chunk will meet it (the build plan or `.prawduct/.handoff-notes.md`), or it is not a deferral, it is a drop. What one more round costs here is unavailable (only 1 timed verify-resolutions round(s) recorded — too few to quote as this repo's price) — that is a missing number, not a small one.
